transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Valence SRE), Ethan Cole (Valence ML Eng), Amanda Lee (Product), Jason (procurement)

Summary (auto): quick checkin on gateway creds, early perf anomalies, and securing keys.

[00:00] Maya: okay hi everyone thanks for hopping on, were on for the weekly poc sync, quick agenda - creds, traffic profile, perf bursts, security questions, next steps.
[00:18] Priya: hi, thanks. quick note we pushed the staging VPC config but havent added the redwood ip allow list yet. sorry about that.
[00:30] Diego: no worries, do you have the CIDR and the egress rules? sometimes the gateway requires both 443 and the health check port.
[00:46] Priya: yep CIDR ready, will paste in the confluence page after this call. also question: do you need a bastion or can we do direct peering?
[01:00] Maya: peering is fine, direct peering preferred for latency reasons. bastion only if your security team mandates an extra hop.
[01:12] Ethan: quick technical Q - for the traffic shaping profile, are you expecting a synthetic token distribution or real production traces? we can provide anonymized traces but want to know the bin sizes.
[01:26] Diego: ideally real traces, but sampled. well run with two distributions: small (chatty short prompts, avg 80 tokens) and long (summaries, 800-1200 tokens). please also include peak 95th percentile bursts.
[01:45] Amanda: and on success criteria, product wants p95 under 300ms for short prompts, p95 under 1.2s for long completions. is that realistic on hosted?
[01:58] Diego: for hosted with caching and prefix KV we have a good chance; if those SLOs are strict you may need a dedicated reservation or quantization tweaks.
[02:10] Priya: by dedicated do you mean reserved GPU pool? curious about cost delta.
[02:17] Maya: yes Dedicated is a reserved pool - lower jitter and prioritization. cost is higher but more consistent latency. we have a pricing scenario I can send after we see perf results.
[02:33] Jason: procurement ask - any special terms for data residency and audit logs? we need audit logs for our SOC 2 audit.
[02:42] Maya: we provide audit logs and retention options; SOC2 compliance attestation available. Diego will share a one-page KMS/HSM integration diagram.
[02:54] Ethan: also curious about tokenization differences - we saw slight token count variance between open tokenizer libs and redwoods tokenizer in early tests.
[03:05] Diego: ah yes tokenizers can drift, especially with special unicode sequences; well include the tokenizer version used in the burst tests. could be the source of cost variance.
[03:20] Priya: ok next: latency outliers from last weeks run - we saw p99 spikes ~2.9s at around 11am, looks correlated with batch size bump.
[03:34] Diego: that matches expected behavior when autoscaling warmup and microbatching align poorly. two mitigations: 1) pin min replicas during business hours, 2) reduce burst size or increase KV cache hit rate.
[03:50] Amanda: how do we measure KV cache hit rate? we need to map to cost savings.
[03:58] Diego: console shows token-level cache stats and hit-rate over time; I'll export a sample CSV. caching can cut token compute up to 40% on stable prompts.
[04:12] Priya: about KMS - we use our cloud KMS and cannot share keys. what integration options do you support?
[04:20] Maya: we support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via customer KMS and HSM; Redwood control plane can be configured to not persist material keys, and audit logs capture key wrap events.
[04:33] Priya: great, please send the diagram.
[04:39] Diego: noted. Ill attach the KMS sketch and the SAML flow.
[04:45] Jason: procurement will need an SLA on uptime for the dedicated scenario - what does that look like?
[04:53] Maya: Dedicated comes with an SLA for throughput and availability; exact numbers depend on the reserved commit. Ill include a sample SLA in the follow-up email.
[05:02] Amanda: fantastic. can we talk about the burst test plan? what inputs do you need from us?
[05:09] Diego: we need two artifacts: 1) a traffic trace CSV with per-request token counts and timestamps (anonymized), and 2) a list of peak hours and concurrency targets. well run 3x bursts: control, medium, heavy, and give raw logs.
[05:27] Ethan: we can export last 30 days of traces and redact PII. will do that by EOD tomorrow.
[05:35] Priya: question: will the burst tests simulate secure traffic through our gateway or via direct test harness?
[05:42] Diego: we'll route through the staging gateway to get real-world TLS and network effects; please keep ACLs permissive to Redwood test IPs for the test window.
[05:54] Amanda: small nit - previously the health checks were failing intermittently due to TLS SNI mismatch. we fixed some certs but want to confirm new certs propagate.
[06:07] Maya: ok maybe a quick check after creds are provisioned.
[06:12] Priya: on the tokenization note - we saw higher token counts for emojis and multi-lingual scripts; any suggestions to normalize?
[06:22] Diego: normalize by pre-processing: replace long unicode clusters, and choose a tokenizer version; also use short prompts prefixing when possible to improve cache hits.
[06:33] Amanda: will product own that normalization? were concerned about changing user-visible inputs.
[06:39] Ethan: product and ML will coordinate; we can instrument observability to see before/after counts.
[06:47] Diego: Ill include instrumentation queries in the export.
[06:54] Maya: switching gears, any blockers this week?
[06:58] Priya: main blocker is granting the staging creds to redwood and getting peering accepted; security review scheduled Wed.
[07:07] Maya: if you want I can join the security review to answer questions on audit logs and key handling.
[07:12] Priya: that would help, yes.
[07:15] Diego: another minor item - we noticed higher memory usage on long context runs in the last test; could be kv cache retention settings. well profile and advise on quantization or chunking.
[07:29] Ethan: ok please check for quantization artifact regressions; earlier we saw slight coherence issues with aggressive quant.
[07:38] Diego: sure well run with fp16 and 8-bit baselines and compare quality metrics on the eval set.
[07:46] Amanda: speaking of evals, wed like a quick regression check against our 150 prompt set after the burst tests. is that doable?
[07:54] Diego: yes we can run the eval set as part of the test harness, will produce a diff report.
[08:01] Priya: plans for timing - when do you expect results?
[08:05] Diego: give us 48 hours after creds + traces are available; so if you supply by Tue morning well have initial results Thu AM.
[08:15] Maya: wrap up then - recap next steps: Priya to add CIDR and accept peering by Mon, Ethan to upload traces, Diego to run bursts and share logs, Maya to send SOC2 + KMS notes and Dedicated pricing scenario.
[08:32] Jason: procurement will review the pricing and come back with questions - expect an email.
[08:38] Maya: perfect. one more ask: can we get a point of contact for security review? direct email?
[08:45] Priya: yes, sec-ops alias secops@valence.example.com. add them to the confluence page.
[08:52] Maya: great, Ill do that. thanks everyone, talk soon.
